In \(\mathfrak E_3\), the two arrays \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) are nonnegative, have \((D(0),R(1))\) margins \(f^-\) and \(f^+\), have \((D(1),R(1))\) margin \(\mu_1^\star\), and put mass only on \(D(0)\leq D(1)\); with \(R(0)=\infty\), each is therefore a feasible full-law lift preserving both displayed within-arm tables.  The displayed row sums, column sums, and complete chain-load matrices certify every marked-capacity constraint.  The exact coordinate intervals are \(	heta_

u(2,2)\in[1/10,1/2]\), and \(	heta_
u(3,3)\in[1/5,4/5]\).  For an arbitrary feasible \(f_{ij}\), \(\ell_\star(

u)\geq-1/20\).  The arrays \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) attain these endpoints, so the sharp interval is \([-1/20,1/4]\), strictly inside the coordinate rectangle \([-3/20,7/20]\).  More precisely, fix a nonnegative symmetric \(C^1\) density \(\varphi\) supported on \((-1,1)\), let \(0<\delta<1/8\), and set \(\varphi_\delta(u)=\delta^{-1}\varphi(u/\delta)\), \(b_\delta=\|\varphi_\delta\|_\infty\), \(l_\delta=\|\varphi_\delta'\|_\infty\), \(M_\delta=\max\{b_\delta,b_\delta^2\}\), and \(L_\delta=\max\{l_\delta,2b_\delta l_\delta\}\).  Replacing the finite atoms by these separated bumps, and using a common death-bump draw when the two death categories agree, gives two full laws with the same strict support separation.  These laws belong to every declared envelope class satisfying \(M\geq M_\delta\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta\); hence there is a nonempty bounded-Lipschitz envelope regime, and within each such fixed regime the separation persists on a relatively open neighborhood of the displayed mixture weights.  No smooth-witness claim is made for arbitrary smaller fixed envelopes.
body.justification: The exact atomic certificate proves strict joint support, and explicit kernel norms identify a nonempty bounded-Lipschitz regime where the separation persists.
body.gap: A smooth bump construction does not satisfy arbitrary preassigned density and Lipschitz envelopes; the corrected result exposes the required constants instead of silently strengthening the class.
body.consumer: Users can check whether their envelope audit contains the smooth witness and can still use the unconditional atomic support certificate when it does not.
body.proof_tex:
The proof is an exact finite-table certificate followed by a quantitatively delimited smoothing construction.  All probabilities are conditional on the sole value of \(X\).  Since \(R(0)=\infty\), the control numerator is zero at every finite readmission threshold.  The four control death rows each have mass \(1/4\), so
\[
S(1)=\frac34,\qquad S(2)=\frac12,\qquad S(3)=\frac14.                \tag{19}
\]
Thus \(0<\eta\leq1/4\) puts \((1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\) in \(\mathcal H_\eta\).

For a feasible projected table \(f=(f_{ij})\), define
\[
A_1=\sum_{i>0}f_{i0},\qquad
A_2=\sum_{\substack{i>1\\j\leq1}}f_{ij},\qquad
A_3=\sum_{j\leq2}f_{3j}.
\]
The singleton capacities from the quadratic chain theorem and the fixed row demands imply
\[
\frac1{20}\leq A_1\leq\kappa^\star_{00}=\frac15,                    \tag{20}
\]
because the other three first-cut columns have total capacity \(7/10\), whereas the demand beyond that cut is \(3/4\).  Likewise,
\[
\frac1{20}\leq A_2\leq\kappa^\star_{10}+\kappa^\star_{11}=\frac14,  \tag{21}
\]
because the second-cut demand is \(1/2\) and columns \(2,3\) have total capacity \(9/20\).  Finally,
\[
\frac1{20}\leq A_3\leq
\kappa^\star_{20}+\kappa^\star_{21}+\kappa^\star_{22}=\frac15,      \tag{22}
\]
where the lower bound follows from \(A_3=1/4-f_{33}\) and \(f_{33}\leq\kappa^\star_{23}=1/5\).

The displayed flows \(f^+\), \(f^-\), and \(f^+\) attain the three upper endpoints, and \(f^-\) attains the lower endpoint in (22).  For the remaining lower endpoints, define
\[
100g^{(1)}=
\begin{pmatrix}
20&0&0&5\\0&15&5&5\\0&0&5&20\\5&5&5&10
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
100g^{(2)}=
\begin{pmatrix}
20&0&0&5\\0&20&0&5\\0&0&10&15\\5&0&5&15
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both have the required row and column margins.  Their complete singleton chain loads, multiplied by \(100\), are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}5&20&15&35\\5&5&10&30\\5&5&5&10\end{pmatrix}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\begin{pmatrix}5&20&15&35\\5&0&15&30\\5&0&5&15\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Each matrix is entrywise bounded by \(100\kappa^\star\).  The quadratic chain theorem therefore makes both tables feasible, with \(A_1(g^{(1)})=1/20\) and \(A_2(g^{(2)})=1/20\).  The image of the convex flow polytope under each linear coordinate is an interval, so (20)--(22) are the exact intervals.  Dividing by (19), whose denominators are positive, gives
\[
\theta_\nu(1,1)\in\left[\frac1{15},\frac4{15}\right],\quad
\theta_\nu(2,2)\in\left[\frac1{10},\frac12\right],\quad
\theta_\nu(3,3)\in\left[\frac15,\frac45\right].                   \tag{23}
\]

Direct summation of the listed nonzero lift entries gives
\[
100\left(\sum_hq^-_{ihj}\right)_{ij}
=\begin{pmatrix}10&0&10&5\\0&10&5&10\\15&5&0&5\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix}
=100f^-,
\]
\[
100\left(\sum_hq^+_{ihj}\right)_{ij}
=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&10&10\\10&15&0&0\\0&0&0&25\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix}
=100f^+,
\]
and, for both signs,
\[
100\left(\sum_iq^\pm_{ihj}\right)_{hj}
=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&0&5\\5&10&0&5\\5&5&10&10\\10&5&5&20\end{pmatrix}
=100\mu_1^\star.                                                     \tag{24}
\]
Every listed entry is nonnegative.  Both projected tables have row sums \((25,25,25,25)/100\) and column sums \((25,20,15,40)/100\); attaching \(R(0)=\infty\) therefore gives \(\mu_0^\star\).  Every positive triple has \(i\leq h\), proving \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  Every finite treated readmission category in a positive cell has \(r_j^\star<d_h^\star\), and the control event-order restriction is vacuous.  The complete singleton chain loads are
\[
100\left(\sum_{i>k}f^-_{ij}\right)_{kj}
=\begin{pmatrix}15&20&5&35\\15&10&0&25\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
100\left(\sum_{i>k}f^+_{ij}\right)_{kj}
=\begin{pmatrix}20&20&5&30\\10&5&5&30\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both are entrywise bounded by \(100\kappa^\star\).  Every mark set on the finite carrier is a union of singleton columns, so summing these inequalities certifies all event-set capacities.

Using (19) in the signed direction gives
\[
\ell_\star(\nu)=A_1-A_2+A_3=f_{10}-f_{21}+f_{30}+f_{32}.             \tag{25}
\]
Nonnegativity and the first-cut column-zero and third-cut column-two capacities yield
\[
\ell_\star(\nu)
\leq f_{10}+f_{30}+f_{32}
\leq\kappa^\star_{00}+\kappa^\star_{22}=\frac14.                    \tag{26}
\]
The second-cut column-one capacity and the last-row margin give
\[
f_{21}+f_{31}\leq\frac1{10},
\qquad
f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32}=\frac14-f_{33}\geq\frac1{20}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\ell_\star(\nu)
=f_{10}-(f_{21}+f_{31})+(f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32})
\geq-\frac1{20}.                                                      \tag{27}
\]
Direct substitution gives \(\ell_\star(f^-)=-1/20\) and \(\ell_\star(f^+)=1/4\).  The full lifts in (24) attain the endpoints, and their mixtures preserve both margins and all support restrictions.  Hence the sharp signed interval is \([-1/20,1/4]\).

The coordinate rectangle generated by (23) has support endpoints
\[
\frac34\frac1{15}-\frac12\frac12+\frac14\frac15=-\frac3{20},
\qquad
\frac34\frac4{15}-\frac12\frac1{10}+\frac14\frac45=\frac7{20}.
\]
Thus its interval \([-3/20,7/20]\) is strictly larger by \(1/10\) at each endpoint.

It remains to delimit the smooth regime.  Fix a nonnegative symmetric \(C^1\) density \(\varphi\) supported on \((-1,1)\), let \(0<\delta<1/8\), and define
\[
\varphi_\delta(u)=\delta^{-1}\varphi(u/\delta),\quad
b_\delta=\|\varphi_\delta\|_\infty,
\quad l_\delta=\|\varphi_\delta'\|_\infty,
\]
\[
M_\delta=\max\{b_\delta,b_\delta^2\},
\qquad
L_\delta=\max\{l_\delta,2b_\delta l_\delta\}.                     \tag{28}
\]
These constants are finite.  Replace each finite category by the corresponding translated bump and retain every \(\infty\) atom.  In a positive lift cell \((i,h,j)\), use independent death draws when \(i<h\), the same death draw when \(i=h\), and an independent readmission draw.  Distinct death centers are at least one unit apart, so \(2\delta<1\) preserves \(D(0)\leq D(1)\); the smallest compatible finite readmission--death gap is \(1/4\), so \(2\delta<1/4\) preserves \(R(1)<D(1)\).  The control readmission remains \(\infty\).

Every finite-part within-arm density is a convex mixture of translates of either \(\varphi_\delta\) or \(\varphi_\delta\otimes\varphi_\delta\).  The former has sup-norm at most \(b_\delta\) and Lipschitz constant at most \(l_\delta\).  For the latter, the product rule and the mean-value inequality give sup-norm at most \(b_\delta^2\) and Lipschitz constant at most \(2b_\delta l_\delta\).  Convex mixtures do not enlarge these bounds.  Equation (28) therefore proves membership in every declared envelope class with
\[
M\geq M_\delta,
\qquad L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta.                                \tag{29}
\]
This is a nonempty envelope regime; nothing in the construction proves membership when either inequality in (29) fails.

No bump support crosses any threshold \(1,2,3\).  Every numerator, denominator, and cut used in (20)--(27) therefore has its categorical value.  The categorical inequalities remain upper and lower bounds for every smoothed coupling, while the two smoothed full lifts attain the two signed endpoints.  Hence the exact strict support calculation survives smoothing throughout (29).

Finally fix \(\varphi\), \(\delta\), and the incidence pattern, and vary the finitely many mixture weights within the feasible cone.  The relevant threshold support programs have a fixed finite constraint matrix.  Their values are maxima and minima of finitely many affine basic values, hence are continuous and piecewise affine on the feasible weight polytope.  Since each strict gap equals \(1/10\) at the displayed law, both remain positive on a sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood.  The density bounds (29) remain valid because the kernels are fixed and the mixture weights sum to one.  Randomized treatment with probability \(1/2\), degenerate positive \(X\), consistency, and \(C=\tau=3\) give exchangeability, overlap, independent censoring, and \(G_{zx}(u)=1\geq\gamma\) through the full horizon.
